asanas.summary: Classical meditation seat prized for nadi-shuddhi preparation; minimal acute glucose disposal, strong manas/sattva orientation.
asanas.lineageEvidence: Gheranda; Hatha Yoga Pradipika; Shiva Samhita; T2/A1
asanas.insulinGlucose: B0-B1: little acute glucose disposal; possible indirect benefit through reduced arousal and better adherence.
asanas.shariraWellbeing: Axial postural endurance, hip mobility and stable breath/attention. Especially suited to stable meditation.
asanas.manasAyurveda: A1: vata-grounding and prana-manas integration; no direct dhatu or insulin claim.
asanas.safety: Protect knees, hips and ankles; use height/support rather than forcing rotation.

iyengar.therapeuticUse: Meditation base when lotus is unavailable

contraindications.rationale: Forced external rotation may aggravate joint pain

claims.statement: HYP frames steady asana as supporting nadi purification before pranayama.

asanas.summary: Kneeling meditation seat; traditionally tolerated after meals though postprandial insulin evidence is lacking.
asanas.insulinGlucose: B0-B1: little acute glucose disposal; folk post-meal digestive comfort claim plausible but not trial-proven.
asanas.shariraWellbeing: Kneeling axial endurance; may support comfortable upright rest after eating when knees tolerate it.
asanas.manasAyurveda: A1: annavaha and jatharagni association in integrative teaching; not verbatim Charaka.
asanas.safety: Protect knees and ankles; use blanket or bench if compression is excessive.

srotas.mechanism: Upright kneeling abdominal positioning at rest

iyengar.therapeuticUse: Short sits after meals when walking is impossible

contraindications.rationale: Prolonged knee flexion and venous compression

claims.statement: Post-meal comfort seat, not metabolically equivalent to active muscle contraction.

asanas.summary: Strong seated twist; Gheranda T1 agni/digestive claim; no proof of pancreatic insulin stimulation.
asanas.insulinGlucose: B1: modest muscular work; no proof that compression triggers insulin secretion.
asanas.shariraWellbeing: Thoracic rotation and trunk control; traditional disease claims exceed posture-specific evidence.
asanas.manasAyurveda: A1: samana/apana and annavaha-purishavaha hypotheses; avoid literal detox claims.
asanas.safety: Avoid strong closed twists after meals, during pregnancy or with acute disc pain.

contraindications.condition: Recent abdominal surgery or disc herniation
contraindications.rationale: Rotation under load is a recognized back-pain mechanism

claims.statement: Gheranda states this asana increases digestive fire and destroys terrible diseases.

asanas.summary: Posterior-chain fold with one of the clearest classical agni links in the canon.
asanas.lineageEvidence: Gheranda; Hatha Yoga Pradipika; Shiva Samhita related Ugra; T2/A1
asanas.insulinGlucose: B1: passive holds have little glucose-disposal effect; dynamic repetitions recruit more muscle.
asanas.shariraWellbeing: Posterior-chain mobility and down-regulation for some practitioners.
asanas.manasAyurveda: A1: apana-vata/purishavaha association; abdominal compression is not proven endocrine therapy.
asanas.safety: Modify with disc symptoms, neural tension, glaucoma or retinopathy.

iyengar.therapeuticUse: Hamstring mobility and calming sequence end

contraindications.rationale: Forced flexion may worsen neural irritation

claims.statement: Gheranda states this asana increases digestive fire and makes the body slim.

lineageVariants.notes: Gheranda squat seat differs from modern standing chair form

asanas.summary: Large-muscle isometric loading with comparatively strong acute glucose plausibility when held or repeated.
asanas.insulinGlucose: B1-B2: active large-muscle work supports contraction-mediated glucose uptake when held or sequenced.
asanas.shariraWellbeing: Lower-limb strength, balance, proprioception and weight-bearing.
asanas.manasAyurveda: A1: mamsa-asthi support and kapha-meda mobilization; rasavaha/raktavaha demand increases.
asanas.safety: Use support for fall risk; avoid strain or breath holding.

alignmentCues: Arms aligned with ears in full form
iyengar.therapeuticUse: Leg strengthening; post-meal active option when walking unavailable

claims.statement: Sustained quadriceps work plausibly supports contraction-mediated glucose uptake.

asanas.summary: Only standing pose among Gheranda's 32; balance and proprioception training with modest metabolic demand.
asanas.insulinGlucose: B1: metabolic demand varies; usually more neuromotor than glycemic.
asanas.shariraWellbeing: Single-leg balance trains proprioception and attention.
asanas.manasAyurveda: A1: buddhi/indriya coordination and vata stabilization through controlled attention.
asanas.safety: Use wall/chair when fall consequences are meaningful.

iyengar.therapeuticUse: Elder balance protocols as component pose

asanas.summary: Krishnamacharya-lineage standing pose; leg endurance and lateral opening without classical T1 antecedent.
asanas.lineageEvidence: Modern/common; T1/A1 lineage synthesis; B0-B1 posture-specific
asanas.insulinGlucose: B1-B2: active large-muscle work can support contraction-mediated glucose uptake when held.
asanas.shariraWellbeing: Combines leg endurance, lateral hip control and thoracic rotation.
asanas.manasAyurveda: A1: mamsa-asthi support and kapha-meda mobilization.
asanas.safety: Use support for fall risk; avoid strain or breath holding.

iyengar.therapeuticUse: Component in hypertension and back-care trial protocols

contraindications.condition: Uncontrolled hypertension with head below heart

asanas.summary: Upper-limb loading and posterior-chain length; mild inversion without special glycemic advantage.
asanas.insulinGlucose: B0-B1: no special insulin-lowering advantage; hydrostatic changes do not equal metabolic benefit.
asanas.shariraWellbeing: Upper-limb loading, posterior-chain length, proprioceptive challenge.
asanas.manasAyurveda: Traditional pranic claims remain within their own framework; not equated with cerebral perfusion benefit.
asanas.safety: Modify with glaucoma, retinopathy, cervical disease, uncontrolled BP or high fall risk.

iyengar.therapeuticUse: Transition pose and shoulder girdle strengthening

asanas.summary: Integration and recovery pose; minimal glucose disposal, strong down-regulation pathway.
asanas.insulinGlucose: B0-B1: minimal direct glucose uptake; potential indirect benefit via stress/sleep pathways.

asanas.manasAyurveda: A1: vata-pitta calming and ojas-supportive as whole-system inference.
